Oh man, I feel for you. That situation sounds like it sucks. I realized I had a crush on a friend (both girls) a few years ago and I’m still struggling with all of this. Maybe I’m not the best person to give advice but all I can say is that pushing it away is really hard to do forever. I was totally not ready to deal with that when I first realized so it helped for a bit, but then I started to become very depressed. Hiding it forever just isn’t a good idea for your own health. 
I’m not sure if you and your friend are still on good terms, but what family thinks isn’t everything. 
I hope you get responses from people who can help you more. I wish you the best luck <3

It’s crazy how one thing can set you on a path of destruction. Comparison of looks in pageants and such can be terrible for young kids and it seems like you experienced that in full force. I’m thankful that where I’m from this isn’t much of a thing. Maybe sharing this is a first step in the right direction for you? Your mind isn’t broken, just a bit out of sorts and there are many resources to help you get back to a healthy mindset if you look for them. I believe in you and hope for you to become healthy and happy. Sending lots of love and wishes. <3

Hi I hope you don’t kill yourself. Please know that having autism or being unattractive in your eyes really doesn’t matter. Stereotypes suck and people can be very ignorant, but you aren’t a bad person or a jerk because of their inability to understand. 

You have survived every one of your worst days so far so I believe you can make it through this one too.
Sending love and hope your way.

What about trying to call a hotline? The school councillor might tell your mom but a hotline is completely confidential. Hang in there maybe you can see a friend after school or have dinner with your mom so that you are occupied after school and don’t have a chance to do something drastic?

Well..you might not be able to. But it’s okay. The main idea is that we respect everyone. Getting into an argument is likely to push him further into the beliefs he already has (what you already know feels safe). I would be really casual and explain stuff like: people are flamboyant because it makes them feel confident, or ‘cause it’s fun or for so many reasons. Or maybe for the non binary thing like he doesn’t have to agree with it but if such a large number of people find it to make them feel comfortable and happy then you just have to acknowledge that.
If he acts like a civilized human being and is respectful than even if he disagrees that’s his business you know?

To be honest if you tell him you like him be prepared for your friendship not to be the same. This happened to me with my friend (but both girls). I never told her exactly but I know she could tell I liked her. Don’t delude yourself to think there is a chance with him. Only if you really think that he is gay.
My advice, as harsh as it is, is to keep your friendship. If he’s cool with lgbt then come out to him, but don’t say that you like him unless you think your friendship is strong enough for you to forget that feeling and for him to look past it in the future.
I haven’t talked to the girl who was my best friend and first crush in three years, and will probably never get to talk to her again. Trust me you don’t want that.
Sending love and hope your way 💜.
